# @scrylog/opencode-plugin

`@scrylog/opencode-plugin` is an OpenCode plugin that sends session and permission events to the `scrylog` daemon webhook in real time.

This is the recommended OpenCode integration when `scrylog` is running in `hooks` mode.

## When To Use This Plugin

The optional bridge adds owning-session conversation reads, mode discovery, authorized start/queue messages, model selection and native interaction responses. See [Optional conversation and message control](#optional-conversation-and-message-control) for the scope beyond monitoring.

Use this plugin when:

- you want `scrylog` to receive immediate, webhook-driven OpenCode session updates
- you want `hooks` mode, which is the recommended OpenCode mode in `scrylog`
- you run OpenCode inside `tmux` and want the best available pane correlation with `tmux` panes

The plugin forwards events regardless of your environment; `tmux` correlation is optional and only applies when OpenCode runs inside a `tmux` pane.

Do not use this plugin as your primary integration when:

- you are using `opencode.mode: "sse"`
- you want standalone-only OpenCode monitoring through `opencode --port`, `opencode serve`, or `oc`

In `sse` mode, the `scrylog` daemon accepts the HTTP request but ignores the payload and returns:

```json
{ "ok": true, "skipped": "opencode-mode-sse" }
```

## What The Plugin Does

The plugin listens for OpenCode session and permission events and forwards them to:

```text
http://127.0.0.1:7788/api/webhook/opencode
```

If OpenCode is running inside `tmux`, the plugin also tries to write the current OpenCode session ID into the pane option:

```text
@opencode-session
```

That gives `scrylog` an exact signal for correlating the OpenCode session with the `tmux` pane.

## Requirements

- `@scrylog/cli` installed and reachable through the `scrylog` command
- `scrylogd` running
- OpenCode installed
- `opencode.mode` set to `hooks` in `scrylog`
- `tmux` installed if you want pane correlation

## Upgrading to 0.8.0

**When upgrading from scrylog versions earlier than 0.8.0, reinstall the OpenCode hook registrations and refresh OpenCode's plugin cache.** Version 0.8.0 introduces separate server and TUI registrations. Keeping only the old server registration cannot detect a restored idle session without a new native observation or prompt.

OpenCode installs npm plugins into its own cache, independently of globally installed packages. Updating `@scrylog/opencode-plugin` globally does not guarantee that OpenCode loads the new build. Apply this migration once when crossing the 0.8.0 boundary; refreshing the cache is also useful on later upgrades if OpenCode keeps loading an older plugin.

1. **Close the OpenCode processes using the plugin.** Close the relevant TUI windows and fully quit Desktop or stop a separate server if it loads the plugin. Run the following steps from another terminal.
2. **Update both packages and any pinned plugin versions.** After the release is published:

   ```bash
   bun install -g @scrylog/cli@latest
   bun install -g @scrylog/opencode-plugin@latest
   ```

   If `opencode.json[c]` or `tui.json[c]` pins `@scrylog/opencode-plugin@<version>`, update both to the same published build, version 0.8.0 or later. Check project-level overrides too. The installer preserves existing pins; clearing a cache cannot override an old pin. Local source shims must point to the updated source/build and register the TUI module as described under [installation](#3-enable-the-plugin-in-opencode).

3. **Reinstall the registrations with the updated CLI.** This merges the server and TUI entries, preserving unrelated settings, tuples and JSONC comments:

   ```bash
   scrylog opencode hooks install
   ```

4. **Refresh OpenCode's cache before reopening it.** Run `opencode debug paths` to identify the effective cache directory. Remove that cache directory so OpenCode reinstalls its npm plugins and cached dependencies on the next startup. This refresh affects other cached plugins/provider packages too and requires access to their package sources; it does not remove configuration, sessions or credentials from OpenCode's separate data directory.

   | Environment    | Default cache directory                                                   |
   | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
   | macOS / Linux  | `~/.cache/opencode`, or `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/opencode` when set               |
   | WSL            | The Linux-side cache of the OpenCode process running in WSL               |
   | Native Windows | `%USERPROFILE%\.cache\opencode`, unless a custom cache path is configured |

   macOS/Linux/WSL, using the standard XDG cache location:

   ```sh
   rm -rf -- "${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/opencode"
   ```

   Native Windows PowerShell, using the default cache location:

   ```powershell
   $cache = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.cache\opencode'
   if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $cache) {
     Remove-Item -LiteralPath $cache -Recurse -Force
   }
   ```

   If `opencode debug paths` reports a different cache path, use that exact cache directory instead of the defaults above. Keep the **data** directory intact; do not delete `~/.local/share/opencode` to refresh plugins. See OpenCode's [plugin installation](https://opencode.ai/docs/plugins/#how-plugins-are-installed) and [cache troubleshooting](https://opencode.ai/docs/troubleshooting/#clear-the-cache) references.

5. **Restart and verify.** Restart an installed daemon service with `scrylog daemon restart`, or restart foreground `scrylogd` manually. Reopen OpenCode to reinstall/load both plugin parts, then run `scrylog doctor`. Check the server and TUI registrations separately and reconnect MCP hosts after upgrading their CLI process. Registration alone is not proof that the new plugin loaded; inspect OpenCode's startup logs if an old build or a missing `./tui` export is still reported. Native Windows provider control remains unavailable even after registration/cache refresh.

## Installation

### 1. Install the plugin

```bash
bun install -g @scrylog/opencode-plugin
```

You can also use npm:

```bash
npm install -g @scrylog/opencode-plugin
```

### 2. Configure `scrylog` for hooks mode

Create or update `~/.config/scrylog/config.json`:

```json
{
  "opencode": {
    "mode": "hooks"
  },
  "api": {
    "tcpEnabled": true,
    "host": "127.0.0.1",
    "port": 7788
  }
}
```

You can also do this from the main operator CLI:

```bash
scrylog setup
```

Choose OpenCode, then choose `hooks` mode.

The plugin sends HTTP requests, so the default webhook URL requires REST enabled on the shared HTTP listener. Enable it with `scrylog api enable` or `scrylog api setup`, then restart the daemon after saving. MCP-only HTTP exposure does not mount webhooks. On Windows, `SCRYLOG_URL=http://127.0.0.1:7787/api/webhook/opencode` can instead target the local IPC port (`daemon.ipcPort`).

### 3. Enable the plugin in OpenCode

Register the plugin from the main operator CLI:

```bash
scrylog opencode hooks install
```

Or create or update `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` manually:

```json
{
  "plugin": ["@scrylog/opencode-plugin"]
}
```

For OpenCode v1, add the same package to `~/.config/opencode/tui.json` as well. The installer registers both files (including JSONC), but the package must expose `./tui`; installing only the server part cannot detect a reopened idle session. The TUI part reports its current route to its own process-local backend without publishing navigation events. Standalone, tmux and herdr windows use the same mechanism. See [focus architecture and limitations](../../docs/providers/opencode-focus.md), including separate-process `opencode attach` and native Windows action restrictions. Restart OpenCode after changing either plugin part.

For a local source shim such as `~/.config/opencode/plugins/scrylog.ts`, OpenCode v1 needs a second local module for the TUI part. Add `~/.config/opencode/plugins/scrylog-tui.ts`:

```ts
export { default } from 'file:///absolute/path/to/packages/opencode-plugin/src/tui.ts';
```

Then add that file path to the `plugin` array in `~/.config/opencode/tui.jsonc` (or `tui.json`). A file module must default-export the TUI plugin object; exporting the server plugin instead is rejected by OpenCode.

### 4. Start the daemon

```bash
scrylog daemon install
scrylog daemon start
```

Or run the daemon manually in the foreground:

```bash
scrylogd
```

### 5. Start OpenCode

Start OpenCode normally. The plugin loads automatically.

### 6. Verify it works

Open another terminal and check the daemon:

```bash
scrylog api status
scrylog doctor
```

Open the dashboard with `scrylog`; OpenCode sessions should appear when events arrive. For HTTP inspection, use:

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $SCRYLOG_API_TOKEN" http://127.0.0.1:7788/api/sessions
```

Set `SCRYLOG_API_TOKEN`, or configure `api.bearerToken` in the daemon config file, when the daemon requires monitoring authentication. The plugin webhook itself is exempt from API bearer authentication; the plugin sends the API token only on its bridge requests, never on monitoring webhooks. Keep the listener loopback-only unless remote webhook access is intentional.

## Configuration

Monitoring uses the following environment variable. Native control has separate opt-in variables described below.

| Variable      | Default                                      | Purpose                                   |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `SCRYLOG_URL` | `http://127.0.0.1:7788/api/webhook/opencode` | Full webhook URL for the `scrylog` daemon |

### Example: custom daemon port

```bash
SCRYLOG_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9000/api/webhook/opencode opencode
```

If you also moved the `scrylog` API port, make sure your `scrylog` config matches it:

```json
{
  "api": {
    "tcpEnabled": true,
    "host": "127.0.0.1",
    "port": 9000
  }
}
```

### Example: set it in your shell profile

```bash
export SCRYLOG_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9000/api/webhook/opencode
```

## Supported Events

The plugin forwards these OpenCode events:

| Event                | Meaning                                           |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `session.created`    | New session created                               |
| `session.updated`    | Session metadata changed                          |
| `session.deleted`    | Session deleted                                   |
| `session.status`     | State changed, such as `busy`, `idle`, or `retry` |
| `session.idle`       | Explicit idle signal                              |
| `session.error`      | Session error                                     |
| `permission.updated` | Permission prompt state updated                   |
| `permission.asked`   | Permission prompt shown                           |
| `permission.replied` | Permission prompt answered                        |

## Request Format

Each event is sent as:

- `POST`
- `Content-Type: application/json`

Example payload:

```json
{
  "event": "session.status",
  "directory": "/Users/you/projects/my-app",
  "sessionID": "ses_123",
  "status": {
    "type": "busy"
  }
}
```

For `session.created` and `session.updated`, OpenCode may also include richer `info` payloads such as title, timestamps, and `parentID`.

## Hooks Mode Vs SSE Mode

### In `hooks` mode

The daemon uses plugin webhook events as the primary OpenCode signal.

What you get:

- immediate OpenCode state updates
- permission prompt visibility
- better `tmux` correlation when the pane option is available
- child and subagent visibility when OpenCode emits parent session IDs

### In `sse` mode

The daemon ignores this plugin and instead connects to OpenCode over its HTTP server.

Use `sse` mode when you run:

- `opencode --port 4096`
- `opencode serve`
- `oc`

In `sse` mode:

- OpenCode is shown as standalone only
- OpenCode `tmux` panes are hidden in `scrylog`
- monitoring webhooks are ignored; an installed, enabled interaction bridge still operates independently of opencode.mode

SSE itself has no native-control adapter. SSE monitoring plus an active plugin bridge is a mixed integration, not SSE control parity. See the [documented parity gap](../../docs/known-issues/opencode-sse-hooks-parity.md).

## Limitations

- The plugin can only provide exact `tmux` correlation when it can write `@opencode-session` in the active pane.
- OpenCode `attach` inside `tmux` still does not have complete exact-session support without an upstream OpenCode signal.
- If the daemon is down, webhook sends are fire-and-forget and are silently dropped.

## Native interaction bridge

The plugin includes an opt-in native interaction adapter. When either an explicit `SCRYLOG_BRIDGE_TOKEN` export or the daemon config `interactions.bridgeToken` is available, it reuses the **exact lower-level client supplied by OpenCode**, including its in-process fetch, authentication headers, directory routing and interceptors. It never reconstructs an OpenCode localhost client, opens an OpenCode listener, subscribes to external SSE or rewrites provider configuration. Explicitly authorized session messages can submit caller-provided text through this supplied transport; plan responses separately use the fixed continuation described below. Monitoring webhooks and root-only tmux pane binding continue independently.

### Optional conversation and message control

| Feature            | Contract                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Conversation       | Up to 100 messages and 192 KiB of text through the exact observed session's SDK; read-only and not persisted by the daemon                                    |
| Modes and messages | Visible primary/all agents, idle start or active queue via promptAsync; no steering. Discovery and sends require the live owning lease and dispatch preflight |
| Models             | Project-configured provider catalog, paginated preferred/all scopes; available local favorites/recents are read-only ordering hints                           |
| Explicit selection | Optional advertised provider/model/variant only on idle starts; feature-negotiated independently so old plugins cannot silently ignore it                     |

No OpenCode HTTP listener is needed; the daemon bridge still requires a reachable HTTP endpoint. Omitted model preserves native precedence, including independent build/plan agent models, without pinning session current model. A native ACK leaves message delivery unknown and must not be replayed. Queue consumption/ordering, interactive focus and explicit model execution remain pending native acceptance. OpenCode E3 catalog evidence is recorded separately; see the [model contract](../../docs/providers/session-model-selection.md) and [conversation recipe](../../docs/testing/session-conversation-manual.md).

Run `bun run --cwd packages/opencode-plugin test` and `bun run --cwd packages/opencode-plugin check-types` from the repository root. Tests use a real SDK root client with a fake **in-process** fetch and an unreachable nominal base URL. They verify transport/header/directory/interceptor preservation with global fetch forbidden, native permission and question translations, plan tool/path/hash gates, confirmations versus stale/unknown results, local closure, duplicate-operation fencing, report-loss reconnect and poll disposal. ## Troubleshooting

### Plan discovery and bridge deadlines

Changed verified capabilities are published before pending interactions without waiting for command long-poll completion. Content-free incident diagnostics are persisted by default under `~/.local/state/scrylog/diagnostics`, with classified operation/phase/deadline and owner correlation. Bridge failures no longer write directly over the TUI through stderr. After upgrading, restart the daemon and owning OpenCode processes. Use `scrylog diagnostics --session 'opencode:ses_example' --pseudonymize` on the affected host; see [retrospective diagnosis and retention limits](../../docs/testing/incident-diagnostics.md). A missing record does not prove that an error did not occur, and an unknown native write outcome never permits replay.

### Subagents launching `opencode run` generate unwanted notifications

A fresh `opencode run` launched through Bash creates a root session without declaring its supervising agent. Scrylog therefore monitors it independently. Keep standalone monitoring enabled for legitimate local or remote tasks; preserve session ancestry for agent-owned work instead.

**Option 1 — native delegation.** Add this instruction to the rules received by the subagents:

> Para delegar trabajo, utiliza la herramienta nativa `task`. No crees sesiones adicionales de OpenCode mediante Bash, `opencode run`, `opencode serve` o SDK. Si no tienes delegación disponible o alcanzas su límite, devuelve el trabajo al agente padre.

This is a prompt convention, not an enforced restriction. Restart OpenCode after changing agent configuration or instructions.

**Option 2 — explicit child creation.** If the launcher knows the real owning session ID, existing server URL, and working directory, create a child through the OpenCode API/SDK with `parentID`, then continue that child with the CLI:

1. Send `POST /session?directory=<URL-encoded-directory>` with `{"parentID":"ses_actual_owning_subagent","title":"Auxiliary work"}`. Check the response and returned ancestry.
2. Use the returned child ID on the same server and directory:

   ```sh
   opencode run --attach "$SERVER_URL" --dir "$WORKING_DIRECTORY" \
     --session "$CHILD_SESSION_ID" "Perform the auxiliary work."
   ```

3. Confirm completion and read the new assistant result from `GET /session/{childID}/message?directory=<URL-encoded-directory>` if CLI stdout omits it. Use matching API/CLI credentials when authentication is enabled.

The variables above are launcher-supplied placeholders. OpenCode 1.19.5 has no `run --parent` flag, and the Bash context probe did not expose the candidate session/server environment variables checked. Do not infer identity from the latest session, use `--fork`, or fall back to creating a root.

Prompt for agents supplied with reliable launcher context:

> Si necesitas crear una sesión auxiliar de OpenCode, utiliza el servidor y directorio proporcionados y créala mediante SDK/API con `parentID` igual al ID real de tu propia sesión. Ejecuta el trabajo en esa sesión hija. Si utilizas `opencode run`, continúa la hija ya creada mediante `--attach` y `--session`, sin `--fork`. Confirma que terminó y recoge su resultado; si stdout no contiene la respuesta, consulta los mensajes de esa sesión. No inventes el ID del padre, no elijas la sesión más reciente ni crees una sesión raíz como alternativa. Si no dispones del contexto necesario, devuelve la delegación al agente padre.

The explicit-child flow passed a real CLI/plugin notification experiment with OpenCode **1.19.5 on macOS**, using a local deterministic model fixture: the root control notified once, while child completions did not notify independently. It requires no scrylog code change. Final text was absent from CLI stdout, so completion was verified through persisted messages and state transitions. Autonomous prompt compliance, live SSE, and Linux/Windows execution were not validated.

The plugin forwards ancestry; scrylog suppresses independent child-session notifications. Children can still appear in the dashboard, and their input requests can propagate to a root-task notification. For agents freely choosing Bash commands without explicit launcher context, prefer option 1.

See the [complete workaround guide](https://github.com/scrylog/scrylog/blob/main/docs/known-issues/opencode-nested-run-notifications.md) and [validation evidence](https://github.com/scrylog/scrylog/blob/main/docs/testing/opencode-nested-run-notifications.md).

### The plugin is installed but OpenCode sessions do not appear

Check all of the following:

| Check               | Command or setting                                                       |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Daemon and mode     | `scrylog doctor` reports reachable daemon and `OpenCode mode: hooks`     |
| REST exposure       | `scrylog api status`; the shared HTTP webhook needs REST enabled         |
| Plugin registration | OpenCode config includes `"plugin": ["@scrylog/opencode-plugin"]`        |
| Destination         | `SCRYLOG_URL` points to the correct full webhook URL                     |
| HTTP listener       | `curl http://127.0.0.1:7788/api/health` succeeds for the default address |

### The daemon says webhook events were skipped

Your daemon is probably running with `opencode.mode: "sse"`. Switch it to `hooks` if you want this plugin to drive OpenCode updates.

### I want standalone-only OpenCode monitoring instead

Do not use this plugin as the primary integration. Set `opencode.mode` to `sse` in `scrylog` and start OpenCode with a reachable HTTP endpoint or use `oc`.
